properties.digitized_from: Real block boundary from real street geometry (src/block_fit.py load_blocks(), trimmed against src/street_geometry.py's fuller street buffer).
properties.digitization_method: ADDED 2026-09-19 for the block-by-block plan walk-through (docs/briefs/mission_bay_block_inventory.csv), per the Mission Rock transform-and-register precedent for unbuilt blocks. Drawn in the plan's own park-green color, distinct from the surrounding blue UCSF blocks -- registered as a future open space, not a building site. Currently a landscaped lawn with trees, satellite-confirmed, not a formally named park in any source found. CORRECTED 2026-09-19 (same day): owner has been on site and confirms this is a completed park, not still-planned open space -- status changed from 'planned' to 'complete'. In hindsight this should have been flagged as a question rather than guessed: the satellite/building-footprint evidence gathered (landscaped lawn with trees, no dirt, no structure) was consistent with either a finished small park or an interim-landscaped future site, and that ambiguity should have gone to the owner instead of being resolved by assumption. A follow-up address/parcel lookup (DataSF Assessor Parcels + Building Footprints) found no building footprint on the site and traced the dominant underlying parcel to a retired 1998 'COMMON_AREAS' placeholder (blklot 8799TBA3, dropped 2005) plus edge fragments of the same scattered UCSF campus parcel already flagged for block 17AB -- consistent with open, non-built land, but that check does not by itself establish 'complete' vs 'planned'; it was the owner's own on-site visit that settled it.
properties.accuracy_caveat: PARTIALLY REAL -- the outer boundary is a real polygonized city block from real street geometry, not hand-traced. No internal A/B split needed (this label is a single block).
properties.notes: Owner confirmed on site (2026-09-19) that this park is complete. No building footprint here (satellite- and building-footprint-confirmed); the OCII plan's own Dec 2019 Land Use Map designates this block's future land use as park (shown in park-green). No specific project name, developer, or completion date was found in this pass -- if the owner has one, it would be a useful addition.
